Guys, this may not be the right time to push too many lots into USDJPY, as it's consolidating into this narrow range and can easily go both ways just like it did this US session. Lighter exposure is better - once we have a strong push through either side on hourlies we can increase the lot size as we secure some of the early positions.

Im still long on the same setup as yesterday, tightened a bit the stops around 157.70. Signal short-term is LONG, key dynamic levels on my charts range from 158.05 to 157.77, so my stop looks well protected technically, at least in short-term. Targets are 158.90 & 160.40 but will take profits progressively, as I have several entries.

My system signal SHORT comes at around 157.70-157.60, if it goes there and price allows for a pullback I will reverse.

It's a patience game now, being able to hold on to our bets if successful & accept defeat quickly if the market proves us wrong.

Same here, stopped 158.10 on average, lost a few pips. Now reversed to small shorts, although on my system the signal remains LONG (!).
I'm betting on a bounce from the H4/D1 resistance @158.40, which on a break of the next levels (158.06, 157.80) may give us the breakout we've been looking for.
Anticipating a bit the short because I want to add another 1/2 position to this setup if it confirms & later tonight the volatility may be very high, it's good to have a small exposure from a good level. But I keep stops right above 158.40 & will not move them if price gets near, I want to stay open for a change in direction & not manage losing positions when the setup is still very hazy.

I switched my USD/JPY position from predominantly long to short yesterday, but the high volatility is making things difficult (the yellow band indicates a "squeeze" phase). However, looking closely, the price spiked outside the band and then retraced, so the key is simply to time the entry correctly on a shorter timeframe.
